message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.5","text":"What, then, must be done but this? I will travel to Egypt, befriend the hierophants and prophets of the inner sanctuaries, and, after searching for and finding a magician, persuade him with a great deal of money to perform a raising up of a soul (what is called necromancy), while I inquire as though about some particular matter. But the inquiry will be about learning whether the soul is immortal. It will be mine to know the soul’s answer—that it is immortal—not from its speaking, or even from hearing it, but merely from its being seen, so that, after seeing it with my own eyes, I may have a self-sufficient and adequate conclusion, from the mere fact that it appeared, that it exists. Then the obscure words belonging to hearing will no longer be able to overturn what belongs peculiarly to the eyes. Nevertheless, I put this very consideration before a philosopher of my acquaintance, who advised me on many grounds not to dare such a thing. “For if the soul does not heed the magician,” he said, “you will live with a guilty conscience because you acted against the laws that forbid people to do these things. But if it does heed him, then, besides your living with a guilty conscience, I think that the concerns of piety will no longer prosper for you, though it was for their sake that you dared it. For they say that the divine is hostile toward those who harass souls at the dissolution of dead bodies.” When I heard this, I became more hesitant about attempting such a thing, but I did not abandon the plan I had formed from the beginning. Rather, as one whose impulse had been obstructed, I was disheartened.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀναπομπὴν (τὴν λεγομένην νεκρομαντείαν)","chosen":"a raising up of a soul (what is called necromancy)","rationale":"ἀναπομπή conveys an upward sending or raising; the parenthetical phrase explicitly identifies the practice as necromancy."},{"source_quote":"αὐτάρκη καὶ ἱκανὴν ἀπόφασιν","chosen":"a self-sufficient and adequate conclusion","rationale":"Preserves both coordinated adjectives and takes ἀπόφασις as a settled conclusion."},{"source_quote":"τὰ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ἴδια","chosen":"what belongs peculiarly to the eyes","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between the eyes’ distinctive evidence and words received through hearing."},{"source_quote":"δυσσυνειδήτως βιώσεις","chosen":"you will live with a guilty conscience","rationale":"The adverb describes living with an adversely burdened conscience."},{"source_quote":"τῇ λύσει θανόντων σωμάτων","chosen":"at the dissolution of dead bodies","rationale":"Retains the image of bodily loosening or dissolution without importing a more specific anthropology."},{"source_quote":"ὀκνηρότερος μὲν πρὸς τὸ τοιοῦτον ἐγχειρῆσαι ἐγενόμην","chosen":"I became more hesitant about attempting such a thing","rationale":"The comparative marks increased reluctance to undertake the proposed act."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.6","text":"And, so that I may not recount such things to you at great length, while I was amid so many thoughts and affairs, a report arose quietly during the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Taking its beginning from the spring equinox, it continually grew and, like a truly good messenger of God, traveled throughout the world, unable to bear keeping God’s will silent. Continually, therefore, it became more widespread and greater, saying that once a certain man in Judea, having begun at the spring equinox, was proclaiming to the Jews the kingdom of the eternal God, which he said any one of them would enjoy if he first set his way of life right. And so that he might be believed—that, being full of divinity, he was doing these things—he performed many marvelous signs and wonders by command alone, as one who had received the authority from God. For he makes the deaf hear and the blind regain their sight; he makes those with deformed limbs walk and sets the lame upright; he drives away every disease and puts every demon to flight. Even lepers and people with scabies depart healed merely by gazing intently at him from a distance. Dead people who are brought forward are raised, and there is nothing that he is unable to do. Indeed, the farther time advanced, the truth of the matter—no longer the report, I mean—became much greater and more firmly established through an increasing number of visitors. For by then gatherings were even being held in various places for deliberation and inquiry into who the one who had appeared might be and what he intended to say.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐξ ἐαρινῆς τροπῆς","chosen":"from the spring equinox","rationale":"The seasonal τροπή is understood as the spring turning point, conventionally the equinox."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀγαθὴ θεοῦ ἄγγελος","chosen":"like a truly good messenger of God","rationale":"The report is personified as an ἄγγελος; “messenger” preserves the comparison without requiring a celestial being."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ βούλημα σιγᾶν στέγειν μὴ δυναμένη","chosen":"unable to bear keeping God’s will silent","rationale":"Takes στέγειν with the infinitive σιγᾶν in the sense of enduring or bearing continued silence."},{"source_quote":"προκατορθώσῃ τὴν πολιτείαν","chosen":"first set his way of life right","rationale":"προκατορθόω conveys prior rectification, while πολιτεία here concerns conduct or manner of life."},{"source_quote":"θειότητος γέμων","chosen":"full of divinity","rationale":"Preserves the abstract noun θειότης and the image of being filled with it."},{"source_quote":"κυλλοὺς γὰρ ποιεῖ ἀκούειν","chosen":"the deaf hear","rationale":"This quotation is not used for the rendering; the supplied sequence itself appears elsewhere as κωφοὺς γὰρ ποιεῖ ἀκούειν, so no lexical decision is based on this wording."},{"source_quote":"κυλλοὺς ποιεῖ περιπατεῖν, χωλοὺς ἀνορθοῖ","chosen":"he makes those with deformed limbs walk and sets the lame upright","rationale":"Uses distinguishable expressions for κυλλοί and χωλοί rather than collapsing the two clauses."},{"source_quote":"λεπροὶ ψωροὶ","chosen":"lepers and people with scabies","rationale":"Treats the two skin-condition terms as distinct descriptions; ψωροί denotes people with an itching or scabby condition."},{"source_quote":"συστήματα κατὰ τόπους","chosen":"gatherings were even being held in various places","rationale":"σύστημα denotes an organized gathering or assembly, distributed here across different locations."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὴν. τοῦ ἀιδίου θεοῦ","issue":"The supplied print has a full stop between the article and its dependent genitive phrase. The syntax requires the words to be construed continuously; this is an apparent editorial punctuation defect, not an OCR claim.","proposed_reading":"τὴν τοῦ ἀιδίου θεοῦ","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"κυλλοὺς γὰρ ποιεῖ ἀκούειν","issue":"This sequence does not occur in the supplied source; the supplied reading is κωφοὺς γὰρ ποιεῖ ἀκούειν. It must not be used as evidence.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"1.7","text":"Then, once in that same year, at the autumn equinox, someone stood publicly and cried out, saying, “Men of Rome, listen! The Son of God is present in Judea, promising eternal life to all who desire it, if they live in accordance with the will of the Father who sent him. Therefore change your way of life from worse things to better, from temporary things to eternal. Know that there is one God, the heavenly one, whose world you inhabit unjustly before his righteous eyes. But if you change and live according to his will, then, after being carried into another age and becoming eternal, you will enjoy his inexpressible good things. If, however, you disobey, your souls, after the dissolution of the body, will be cast into the place of fire, where, being punished eternally, they will reorient themselves to no avail. For each person’s present life is the time for reorientation.” When I heard these things, I was distressed that no one from among so many crowds, after hearing so momentous an announcement, had said, “I will travel to Judea so that I may see whether this man is speaking the truth when he says these things.” For the Son of God had come to Judea, revealing the will of the Father who sent him for the sake of a good and eternal hope, especially since what they say he proclaims is no small matter. For he firmly declares that the souls of some, being eternal, will enjoy eternal good things, whereas the souls of others, after being cast into unquenchable fire, will be punished forever.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς αὐτῷ τῷ ἔτει","chosen":"in that same year","rationale":"The phrase locates the event within that same year; the precise nuance of πρός is not represented as a separate spatial relation in English."},{"source_quote":"ἐν φθινοπωρινῇ τροπῇ","chosen":"at the autumn equinox","rationale":"As with the preceding spring τροπή, the seasonal turning point is understood as the equinox."},{"source_quote":"Ἄνδρες Ῥωμαῖοι","chosen":"Men of Rome","rationale":"Preserves both the direct address ἄνδρες and the identification of the audience as Romans."},{"source_quote":"μεταβάλλεσθε τὸν τρόπον","chosen":"change your way of life","rationale":"The verb is μεταβάλλω, not μετανοέω, and τὸν τρόπον identifies the manner or course of life being changed."},{"source_quote":"ἀπὸ τῶν προσκαίρων ἐπὶ τὰ αἰώνια","chosen":"from temporary things to eternal","rationale":"Preserves the substantival contrast between what lasts only for a time and what is eternal."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀπορρήτων αὐτοῦ ἀγαθῶν","chosen":"his inexpressible good things","rationale":"ἀπόρρητος can describe what is not to be spoken or cannot be expressed; “inexpressible” suits the promised divine benefits."},{"source_quote":"ἀνωφέλητα μετανοήσουσιν","chosen":"they will reorient themselves to no avail","rationale":"Uses the supplied terminology for μετανοέω while preserving the explicit claim that this postmortem reorientation is ineffective."},{"source_quote":"ὁ γὰρ τῆς μετανοίας καιρὸς ἡ νῦν ἑκάστου ζωὴ τυγχάνει","chosen":"For each person’s present life is the time for reorientation","rationale":"Uses the corresponding terminology for μετάνοια without adding a destination absent from the Greek."},{"source_quote":"τὸν αἰῶνα κολασθήσεσθαι","chosen":"will be punished forever","rationale":"The accusative duration expression presents the punishment as continuing throughout the age, rendered idiomatically as “forever.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"σώματος·λύσιν","issue":"The supplied print has a medial stop between the dependent genitive σώματος and λύσιν. The translation construes the phrase continuously; this is treated as an apparent editorial punctuation defect, not as an OCR error.","proposed_reading":"σώματος λύσιν","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ","issue":"The discourse force of the consecutive particles ὡς ὅτι is uncertain. The translation takes them as introducing an explanatory assertion, but does not propose changing the supplied wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"1.8","text":"As I said these things about others, I also spoke to myself, saying, “Why do I blame others when I am under the same charge of negligence? Rather, I will set out for Judea, after first putting my life in order.” Yet, after I had resolved on this course, a long period of delay followed, because the affairs of life were difficult to break free from. At last, then, I reflected in this way on the nature of life: by entangling those who are eager to act in hope, it lies in wait for them. I also considered how much time I had somehow been drawn in by stealth, tossed about by hopes, and that, while occupied in this way, we human beings die. Leaving everything of mine just as it happened to be, I set out for Portus. After reaching the harbor and putting out to sea, I was carried by the hostility of the winds to Alexandria instead of Judea. Then, detained there by a lack of winds, I associated with the philosophers and related the accounts concerning the report and the man who had appeared in Rome. But they answered, “We do not know the man who appeared in Rome. Concerning the one who was in Judea and whom the report called the Son of God, however, we too have heard from many who came from there, and we have learned about all the wonders he performed by speaking.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρότερον τὸν ἐμὸν διαθεὶς βίον","chosen":"after first putting my life in order","rationale":"διατίθημι here indicates arranging or settling one’s life and affairs before departure."},{"source_quote":"τῶν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων δυσεκλύτων ὄντων","chosen":"because the affairs of life were difficult to break free from","rationale":"Preserves both the practical affairs denoted by βιωτικά and the difficulty of disengagement expressed by δυσεκλύτων."},{"source_quote":"ἐλπίδι ἐμπλέκων τοὺς σπεύδοντας ἐνεδρεύει","chosen":"by entangling those who are eager to act in hope, it lies in wait for them","rationale":"Retains the paired images of entanglement and ambush used to characterize life."},{"source_quote":"τὰ πάντα μου ὡς ἔτυχεν ἀφεὶς","chosen":"leaving everything of mine just as it happened to be","rationale":"Preserves the sense that Clement departed without first bringing his possessions or affairs into an orderly condition."},{"source_quote":"εἰς Πόρτον","chosen":"for Portus","rationale":"Πόρτος is treated as the proper name of the port settlement rather than translated generically."},{"source_quote":"ἀνέμων ἔχθραις","chosen":"by the hostility of the winds","rationale":"Retains the source’s personifying image rather than reducing it to merely adverse weather."},{"source_quote":"ἀνέμων ἀπορίᾳ","chosen":"by a lack of winds","rationale":"ἀπορία here indicates a deficiency or absence of wind that prevents onward sailing."},{"source_quote":"περὶ πάντων ὧν λαλῶν ἐποίει θαυμασίων","chosen":"about all the wonders he performed by speaking","rationale":"Takes the participle λαλῶν instrumentally, while acknowledging that contemporaneous “as he spoke” is also grammatically possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ. ὃν ποτε","issue":"The supplied full stop interrupts the correlative expression οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καί and separates it from the further object of reflection. The translation construes the expression continuously; this is an apparent editorial punctuation defect, not an OCR claim.","proposed_reading":"οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃν ποτε","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος","issue":"The construction is semantically difficult, especially the force of εἰσεκλάπην with the accusative χρόνον. The translation understands Clement as having been drawn in by stealth for a length of time while being tossed by hopes, but the precise sense remains unresolved.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
